patent.statute: The Patents Act, 1970 & The Patents Rules, 2003 (as amended 2024)
patent.authority: Controller General of Patents, Designs and Trade Marks (CGPDTM), DPIIT
patent.term_of_protection: 20 years from the date of filing

startup_benefits.fee_concession: 80% rebate on official filing, publication, and examination fees for DPIIT recognized startups and MSMEs.
startup_benefits.expedited_examination: Rule 24C allows Startups to file Form 18A for fast-track examination (target grant within 1 year).

statutory_forms.name: Application for Grant of Patent
statutory_forms.description: Basic bibliographic details of applicant and inventors.

statutory_forms.name: Provisional or Complete Specification
statutory_forms.description: Title, description, abstract, and claims (for complete specification). Up to 30 pages and 10 claims.

statutory_forms.name: Statement and Undertaking under Section 8
statutory_forms.description: Details of corresponding foreign applications filed.

statutory_forms.name: Declaration as to Inventorship
statutory_forms.description: Submitted with complete specification identifying true inventors.

statutory_forms.name: Request for Early Publication
statutory_forms.description: Publishes application in official gazette within 1 month instead of waiting 18 months.

statutory_forms.name: Request for Examination
statutory_forms.description: Normal examination request (due within 31 months of priority date under 2024 rules).

statutory_forms.name: Request for Expedited Examination (Startups)
statutory_forms.description: Fast-track examination for DPIIT recognized startups. Grant within 6-12 months.

statutory_forms.name: Form of Authorization of a Patent Agent
statutory_forms.description: Power of attorney if filing through registered patent attorney.

statutory_milestones.action: File Complete Specification (Form 2) within 12 months. Non-extendable!
Standard publication at 18 months (or 1 month if Form 9 filed).
Must file Form 18 or 18A within 31 months from priority date.
Submit arguments, claim amendments. Extendable by 3 months via Form 4.
Patent granted. Annual renewal fees payable from 3rd year onwards.

trademark.statute: The Trade Marks Act, 1999 & Trade Marks Rules, 2017

startup_benefits.fee_concession: 50% rebate on official application fee (₹4,500 e-filing fee for Startups/Individuals vs ₹9,000 for large companies).

statutory_forms.name: Application for Registration of Trademark
statutory_forms.description: Filing of wordmark, device mark (logo), 3D mark across Nice Classification classes 1 to 45.

statutory_forms.name: Application for Amendment / Extension / Certified Copy
statutory_forms.description: Used for clerical amendments, expedited processing, or extension requests.

statutory_forms.name: Renewal of Registration
statutory_forms.description: Payable every 10 years to maintain trademark validity.

common_classes_for_startups.scope: Computer software, mobile applications, downloadable software, hardware.
Advertising, business management, e-commerce marketplace services, online retail.
Financial services, banking, payment processing, lending, fintech.
Software as a Service (SaaS), IT consulting, cloud computing, technology design.

copyright.software_protection: Computer programs/source code are protected as 'literary works' under Section 2(o). Source code and object code extracts must be deposited.
